atoms.claim: Unscaled flux compactness generally unavailable for large weights.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.FluxNoncompactness.example_action_eq_frobenius
mappings.local_proposition: Unscaled flux compactness generally unavailable for large weights.
mappings.context: Arbitrary real scale sequence tau_j→atTop; finite prefixes need not be positive because proofs work eventually. Original compact interval/native Good path. Exact cost requires tau>0.; Exact cost||J||F²/(2tau), Frobenius variation sqrt(tau)||J||F. Actual gap→0; every StrictMono subsequence and every native candidate fails original signed weak-star convergence via actual continuous constant flux coordinate.
application: Actual example good paths have actions and minimum gaps→0 for arbitrary tau_j→infinity, but every strict subsequence fails signed weak-star convergence and true Frobenius variation diverges. This is an existential obstruction, not denial of compactness under additional hypotheses.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.Examples.rotWeight_eq
mappings.local_proposition: Rotating scalar transport can jump.
mappings.context: Actual closed unit disk, scalar gradOp; epsilon>0,pi*epsilon≤sin(theta),delta>0 for lower certificate; epsilon≤1/25 withtheta=sqrtepsilon gives displayed family.; Native fulltest lower4; literal stationary square masses; singular horizontal moving atom and zero dummy retain true measures/action≤1/2.
application: Scalar rotating family theta=sqrt epsilon,0<epsilon<=1/25 has native value4, target singular weight admits value<=1/2; rotating reaction limits additionally vary with direction. Paper scope is failure of general value continuity, not contradiction of finite relative-comparison theorem.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.GenericBridges.closure_open_setup
mappings.local_proposition: Δ=P1−P0, P_s=P0+sΔ.
mappings.context: All dimensions arbitrary Nat. Topological Radon theorem requires metric compact Borel domain. Reaction square completion needs symmetric H, but no mass invertibility. RegMap identities use genuine PSDSqrt, PSD endpoints and δ>0. Hub specialization needs compact native Ω, HubGeometry, entrywise D, symmetric invertible H.; Exact displayed square-completion orientations/constants, actual regularized map and trace equalities. Only forward D0-annihilation exported.; The two-point quadratic tests with signs +1 and -1 give the half-diagonal bound; the two diagonal-to-trace bounds give the final inequality.; Paper H positive definite gives Hᵀ=H.
application: Formal initial factor is H*P0; formal increment is Δ=P1−P0. Then factorPoint H*P0 H*Δ=H*(P0+sΔ); factorMass/factorRate recover literal M and full Z. factorMass_deriv plus factorMassDeriv_eq_sym gives Mdot=(Z+Zᵀ)/2.

atoms.claim: Three pieces contract to common hub, react, expand.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.Hub.hubMoment_nonneg
mappings.local_proposition: Three pieces contract to common hub, react, expand.
mappings.context: Compact native Ω; HubGeometry; actual entrywise operator; symmetric invertible H; r0,r1,r2>0 summing1; t>0.; Actual three-path sum, intermediate endpoint cancellation including reversed flux sign, all-coordinate mass symmetry; action bound exactly M0/(2t²r0)+E/r1+M1/(2t²r2).
application: Three actual pieces are lagPath(initial,0,+1,r0), reactionPath(hubMeasure,r0,r1),lagPath(terminal,1,−1,r2). r0+r1=1−r2 cancels intermediate endpoint pairings. FullR zero on balanced legs; no general fullR reversal assertion required. Additive signed pairing gives action subadditivity.

mappings.context: Compact convex Ω, hub in interior, arbitrary finite PSD endpoint, valid time segment, r>0,sigma=±1,t>0.; Actual signed pushforward, not formal curve shorthand. mappings.name: LiZouTransport.Examples.rotWeight_eq
mappings.local_proposition: Rotations exhibit failures of value continuity.
mappings.context: Actual closed unit disk, scalar gradOp; epsilon>0,pi*epsilon≤sin(theta),delta>0 for lower certificate; epsilon≤1/25 withtheta=sqrtepsilon gives displayed family.; Native fulltest lower4; literal stationary square masses; singular horizontal moving atom and zero dummy retain true measures/action≤1/2.
application: Scalar rotating family theta=sqrt epsilon,0<epsilon<=1/25 has native value4, target singular weight admits value<=1/2; rotating reaction limits additionally vary with direction. Paper scope is failure of general value continuity, not contradiction of finite relative-comparison theorem.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.Examples.Lhoriz
mappings.local_proposition: Norm-divergent sequence disproves magnitude-only convergence.
mappings.context: Arbitrary real sequence t→infinity; t_j≠0 needed only odd upper estimate and holds eventually. Current paper explicitly positive scales ensures all weights PSD.; Exact even endpoint localhval3/8; odd realtbound2/t² on actual balanced path. Native ENNReal nonconvergence to every candidatec, notonlyfinite realnonconvergence.
application: Positive t_j→infinity; altL uses the actual scale at each even/odd index. Exact Frobenius squared=t_j²+1. Even native values>=3/8 and odd<=2/t_j²→0 prove no ENNReal limit.

atoms.claim: Unscaled-flux example separates energy convergence from flux compactness.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.FluxNoncompactness.example_action_eq_frobenius
mappings.local_proposition: Unscaled-flux example separates energy convergence from flux compactness.
mappings.context: Arbitrary real scale sequence tau_j→atTop; finite prefixes need not be positive because proofs work eventually. Original compact interval/native Good path. Exact cost requires tau>0.; Exact cost||J||F²/(2tau), Frobenius variation sqrt(tau)||J||F. Actual gap→0; every StrictMono subsequence and every native candidate fails original signed weak-star convergence via actual continuous constant flux coordinate.
application: Actual example good paths have actions and minimum gaps→0 for arbitrary tau_j→infinity, but every strict subsequence fails signed weak-star convergence and true Frobenius variation diverges. This is an existential obstruction, not denial of compactness under additional hypotheses.

mappings.context: Actual interval compact convex with midpoint hub and unit Lebesgue spatial reference; full native symmetric tests.; Actual constant full coordinate densities(I,aJ,0). Symmetry kills skew flux pairing. Full CE via time FTC. Original RN action and variation proved from arbitrary reference density formula.
application: Actual example good paths have actions and minimum gaps→0 for arbitrary tau_j→infinity, but every strict subsequence fails signed weak-star convergence and true Frobenius variation diverges. This is an existential obstruction, not denial of compactness under additional hypotheses.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.Examples.kbOp
mappings.local_proposition: KB obstruction shows operator affects large-weight limits.
mappings.context: Actual disk,d=n2,k1, rowdivergence, Hidentity. Every1×1transport matrix including all positive scalarweights.; Full native affine diagonal certificate, flux zero, actual endpoint localhval1/4 and all-competitor infimumlower. TotalsI both; Bureszero establishedseparately.
application: KB equal totals I, Bures(I,I)=0, native value>=1/4 for every isotropic scalar transport weight. Smooth separation separately supplies common weak-star uniformly positive endpoint sequence.

atoms.claim: For a finite dominating λ, each original signed coordinate is reconstructed from its measurable integrable RN density.

mappings.name: MatrixTransport.Paper.ExpandedSupport.action_any_finite_reference
mappings.local_proposition: For a finite dominating λ, each original signed coordinate is reconstructed from its measurable integrable RN density.
mappings.context: Finite positive λ dominates all coordinate variations of μ; therefore each signed coordinate has an integrable measurable real RN density with respect to λ.
application: Set z_c=rnDeriv(μ_c,λ), w=Σ_c|z_c|. The canonical reference is λ.withDensity(ofReal w). The existing proof identifies canonical densities as z_c/w a.e.; when w=0 all z_c=0. This is the RN-chain computation in the text, with h=w.

mappings.name: LiZouTransport.ExpandedScalarExamples.scalar_quadratic_square
mappings.local_proposition: For a>0, sx−as²/2=x²/(2a)−a(s−x/a)²/2.
mappings.context: For the positive branch a>0; for the zero branch the scalar supremum is finite, supplied by finite local support cost.
application: Use m=a,z=x,c=s in the scalar helpers. For a=0 the existing quadratic_dual_bound gives x²≤0 from all-s Fenchel inequalities; hence x=0. The reaction branch uses the same argument with full reaction coordinates.

mappings.name: MatrixTransport.Paper.ExpandedTimeSupport.lagPath_totalVariation_timeSlice_zero
mappings.local_proposition: Every coordinate of each actual positive-duration piece has zero total variation on every time slice.
mappings.context: Compact convex domain with interior hub; actual finite signed endpoint coordinates; positive durations r0,r1,r2 with sum1. Exact action additivity itself needs neither PSD endpoint data nor finite action. The continuity equation and endpoint matching additionally use PSD endpoints, symmetric invertible H, entrywise divergence and the Bures reaction factors.
application: Instantiate contraction=lagPath(G,g0,0,1,r0), reaction=reactionPath(dirac(hub),H,W,Delta,r0,r1), expansion=lagPath(G,g1,1,-1,r2). W and Delta are the existing exists_bures_reaction_factor witnesses in HubRecovery. The two cuts are time<r0 and time<r0+r1. Null total variation on junction slices permits those half-open cuts; a common sum-of-variations reference gives disjoint full RN tuples. hubPath_action_eq is for exactly their coordinate sum, with no disjointness hypothesis left to supply. The existing HubRecovery proof proves its symmetry and native continuity equation by adding the three actual coordinatePair identities and cancelling the two equal endpoint pairings.

mappings.context: Compact convex domain with interior hub; actual finite signed endpoint coordinates; positive durations r0,r1,r2 with sum1. Exact action additivity itself needs neither PSD endpoint data nor finite action. The continuity equation and endpoint matching additionally use PSD endpoints, symmetric invertible H, entrywise divergence and the Bures reaction factors.
application: Instantiate contraction=lagPath(G,g0,0,1,r0), reaction=reactionPath(dirac(hub),H,W,Delta,r0,r1), expansion=lagPath(G,g1,1,-1,r2). W and Delta are the existing exists_bures_reaction_factor witnesses in HubRecovery. The two cuts are time<r0 and time<r0+r1. Null total variation on junction slices permits those half-open cuts; a common sum-of-variations reference gives disjoint full RN tuples. hubPath_action_eq is for exactly their coordinate sum, with no disjointness hypothesis left to supply. The existing HubRecovery proof proves its symmetry and native continuity equation by adding the three actual coordinatePair identities and cancelling the two equal endpoint pairings.
